title: Mouse movement
help: Sends a relative movement with Windows SendInput. Positive X moves right; positive Y moves down. Delay postpones the start. Duration 0 or one step sends the whole motion at once; multiple steps distribute the exact total ΔX/ΔY across the duration. For one action per key press, use If key down → On new press. For repeated motion while held, choose While held and Repeat until stopped. A second block with negative deltas can reverse the motion after a Wait. This does not measure or set a game's camera position. Stop with Ctrl+Alt+F7. Use macros only where permitted.

help: Reads PNG, JPEG, BMP, TIFF, GIF, WebP or PDF locally and stores the result in a variable. PDF pages are rendered in grayscale at 200 DPI and passed to Tesseract. Set PDF page to 1–100 for one page or 0 for all pages (up to 20). GIF and WebP work when the installed Tesseract build includes the matching Leptonica decoders. The app verifies the engine and continues without a restart. If UAC is declined or permission is unavailable, setup stops; you can enter the path to an existing tesseract.exe instead. Engine and file paths containing Cyrillic characters use Windows short names when available. Files are never sent over the network. Automatic setup is unavailable on 32-bit Windows. Limits: 32 MiB PDF/input, 32 MiB rendered page image, 100000 output characters and 1–120 seconds total timeout. Password-protected PDFs cannot be OCRed without a password. Example: set the PDF path to scan.pdf and PDF page to 0; Recognize text reads up to 20 pages into ocr_text, separating page results with a page break. Small or blurry text may be misread.

title: Choice dialog
help: Shows a question. Choose the visible button set by name: 0 OK; 1 OK/Cancel; 2 Abort/Retry/Ignore; 3 Yes/No/Cancel; 4 Yes/No; 5 Retry/Cancel. A set number is NOT a result code: Yes returns 6 and No returns 7. The selected set's result codes appear under the field. The icon is also chosen by name. Stopping closes the dialog. Corresponds to DIALOGBOX(message,buttons[,icon]). Title, X/Y and size are set in this block. Leave both X/Y blank to center on screen. Blank dimensions grow to fit the question, starting at 470×190. Explicit width is 360–3000 and height 180–3000 pixels. X/Y are screen coordinates, not graph coordinates.
note: Run once and inspect the execution journal. The featured block records its actions; surrounding blocks prepare input or show the result. This example sets a custom title and screen position X=80, Y=100. Change its position and size in block properties. Blank X/Y centers it; blank dimensions restore the default size.

title: Select option
help: Shows one choice per line (1–100 choices, up to 250 characters each). Press Enter between choices in the block properties. In graph code, those line breaks appear as \n within one value line; the properties show separate choices. A template \& in properties appears as \\& in code because the code also escapes the backslash. Each line may contain a template such as =[(${counter}+2)*3]& units \&: with counter=1 it displays ‘9 units &’. OK returns the chosen 1-based index; cancel or OK without a selection returns 0. Stopping closes the dialog. Set title, X/Y and size in the block. Leave both X/Y blank to center on screen. Blank dimensions grow to fit the question and choices, starting at 465×410. Explicit width is 360–3000 and height 260–3000 pixels. X/Y are screen coordinates, not graph coordinates.
note: Run once and inspect the execution journal. The featured block records its actions; surrounding blocks prepare input or show the result. The first option displays 9 units &: [] evaluates math, & joins text, and \& prints a literal &. In properties, 11 and 22 are separate lines; graph code writes the breaks as \n. This example sets a custom title and screen position X=80, Y=100. Change its position and size in block properties. Blank X/Y centers it; blank dimensions restore the default size.
